subject: hierarchical model takes extremely long to run and the results are not converged

messages.author: f6e5e26ed77eaab6
messages.subject: hierarchical model takes extremely long to run and the results are not converged
parts:
Hi Stan development team members:

I have been trying to get my toy example running using rstan. I have previously fitted the model in WinBUGS and it works fine but now I would like to converted to stan version as I have heard numerous good things about it.

the model I try to fit is a hierarchical model on 7 categories of species where I model their species abundance estimates recorded as interval (a,b) and parameterised as a bivariate vector (midpoints=(a+b)/2, log (range)=log(b-a)) and fit a multivariate normal distribution to each category of species with its own mean vector and variance and covariance matrix.

However, there is an inherent hierarchical structure within the species and thus I impose constraints on midpoints of each species category.
ie: mu_g[1] (midpoints for global species)= mu_cr[1] (midpoints for coral reefs)+mu_m[1] (midpoints for marine) +mu_t[1] (midpoints for terrestrial) +mu_other[1] (midpoints for all other unobserved species). In addition, mu_t[1]=mu_ar[1](midpoints for arthropods) +mu_insects[1] (midpoints for insects).

In addition, we assume a global correlation matrix for all categories of species and the variance covariance matrix is parameterised to be species-specific diagonal matrix containing standard deviation*global correlation matrix*species-specific diagonal matrix containing standard deviation.

In each category, there are some missing values of log(range).

I use LKJ distribution on cholesky factor of global correlation matrix and fit a multi_normal_cholesky( mean vector, cholesky factor of the covariance matrix) and basically use the most conventional priors on my parameters.

The model did run but it took ages to return the output (much longer comparing to WinBUGS) and unfortunately my results are not converged either.

I think my model is relatively simple and it should not take such a long time for HMC to run, I have attached my stan code and dataset, could someone please suggest me how I can improve the model? Perhaps I overlook some of the aspects?

Thanks so much for your help and advice.

my code of running the model, I have already changed acceptance rate and max_treedepth but it still has divergent transitions.

f_hierarchical_var2<-stan(file='full model var v2.stan',data=data,iter=1000,thin=5,chains=4,control =list(adapt_delta=0.9999,max_treedepth=15) )



Jaslene

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] hierarchical model takes extremely long to run and the results are not converged
parts:
Firstly, 1-2 hours for a complex model with hundreds of parameters is
not incredibly long.

Secondly, those parameters with extremely large values are probably
overflowing (the means and quantiles are not consistent) which is
why you’re getting large Rhats.  You’ll want to rescale those in your
model, for example writing

parameters {
  real x_tilde;
  ...
}

model {
   …
   … 100000 * x_tilde ...
   ...
}

Thirdly, the slow speed is coming from the high treedepth.  Coupled
with the divergences this is indicative of nasty curvature in your posterior
which will require a reparameterization.  The manual discusses
reparameterizations of multivariate hierarchical models.

parts:
Hi Michael:

Thanks for your reply. I am actually thinking about imposing additional constraints on parameters.
Specially,  I would add in constraints for lower and upper bounds of interval for each category of species.

As I model interval (a,b) as (midpoints, log(range)) then a=midpoints-exp(log(range))/2 and b=midpoints-exp(log(range))/2

and given internal hierarchical relationships among species then

lower bound of terrestrial= lower bound of arthropods + LB of insects, same for its upper bounds

LB of global= LB of terrestrial + LB of coral reefs + LB of marine + LB of other and same for its upper bounds.

I declare a positive ordered[2] parameter and specify the following

transformed parameters{
  //set up lower and upper bounds for each category and thus transform into constraints in log(range)
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_cr;
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_g;
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_m;
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_insects;
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_ar;
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_t;
 
  positive_ordered[D] bounds_other;

  //assign constraints on lower and upper bounds of terrestrial and global
               
                bounds_cr[1]<-(mu_cr[1]-exp(mu_cr[2])/2);
               
                bounds_cr[2]<-(mu_cr[1]+exp(mu_cr[2])/2);
               
                bounds_m[1]<-(mu_m[1]-exp(mu_m[2])/2);
               
                bounds_m[2]<-(mu_m[1]+exp(mu_m[2])/2);
               
                bounds_insects[1]<-(mu_insects[1]-exp(mu_insects[2])/2);
               
                bounds_insects[2]<-(mu_insects[1]+exp(mu_insects[2])/2);
               
                bounds_ar[1]<-(mu_ar[1]-exp(mu_ar[2])/2);
               
                bounds_ar[2]<-(mu_ar[1]+exp(mu_ar[2])/2);
               
                bounds_other[1]<-(mu_other[1]-exp(mu_other[2])/2);
               
                bounds_other[2]<-(mu_other[1]+exp(mu_other[2])/2);
               
               
                bounds_t[1]<-bounds_insects[1]+bounds_ar[1];
              
                bounds_t[2]<-bounds_insects[2]+bounds_ar[2];
               
                bounds_g[1]<-bounds_t[1]+bounds_cr[1]+bounds_m[1]+bounds_other[1];
              
                bounds_g[2]<-bounds_t[2]+bounds_cr[2]+bounds_m[2]+bounds_other[2];
               
               
              
               
               
}


where mu_cr[1] is the midpoints parameter and mu_cr[2] is its log(range) parameter.

However, the model is syntactically correct but it did not run and had the following errors:





SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'full model var v2' NOW (CHAIN 1).
  [1] "Error : "                                                                                                                                                   
  [2] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                                             
  [3] "validate transformed params: bounds_cr is not a valid ordered vector. The element at 2 is 1.#QNAN, but should be greater than the previous element, 1.#QNAN"
  [4] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"                     
  [5] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."



Any suggestions and advice will be greatly appreciated!!

Thanks and I am looking forward to hearing back.


Jaslene

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] hierarchical model takes extremely long to run and the results are not converged
parts:
That approach looks right in general, but my guess is that those exponentials
are overflowing due to priors that are too diffuse.  I recommend trying to build 
a much smaller model that captures the essence of what you are trying to do, 
firstly to provide an easier model for you to fit first and secondly to facilitate our
understanding of exactly what model you are trying to build.  As it is the model
it too big for us to be able to grasp without a significant time investment.
